beats.story: Something catches in my throat, and I blink far more than necessary. When we pull up to a beautiful little century-old apartment building with a perfect red door, I blink and blink as an attractive brunette in a trendy, oversized wool jacket with clunky boots and heavy makeup trots toward the car. She walks with such a sure-footed stride that I'm half convinced she owns the sidewalk. "I can give her my seat," I offer, my smile as delicate as a porcelain doll. "No, don't worry, Grace's cool. Just stay put." I don't know why I feel the urge to clarify that I'm just as cool. This Grace opens the back door and says, "We're never going to make it unless you book it now. What, did you need them to pave the roads before you could drive here?" Grace's spicy perfume wafts toward me as she settles into the back.
beats.story_cn: 我喉头一哽，眨眼的频率高得离谱。车子停在一栋漂亮的百年小公寓楼前，那扇完美的红门映入眼帘。我眨了又眨，只见一位穿着时髦超大廓形羊毛外套、蹬着笨重靴子、浓妆艳抹的棕发丽人正朝车小跑而来。她步伐笃定得让我恍惚觉得人行道是她的私有领地。“我可以把座位让给她，”我提议道，笑容精致如瓷娃娃。“别，没事，格蕾丝很随和。坐着别动。”不知为何，我竟想辩解自己同样“随和”。格蕾丝拉开后座车门说道：“再不抓紧可就迟了。怎么，难道还得给你把路铺平才肯开过来吗？”她落座后，浓烈辛辣的香水气息朝我扑来。

Cliff looks between his sister and me again. Why am I smiling so hard? "Nice to meet you." My voice is small. What wonderful things has she heard? And how can there be so many? Grace brightens as she settles back into her seat.

Shit, I've volunteered to do the thing where I have to wear shoes that about a thousand other people have worn. As feared, when the bored gentleman working the rental stall proudly slides a previously white-and- green pair across the counter, I am certain the first person to have rented them died from natural causes some years ago. While lacing up on the plasticky cup seats, Cliff shifts toward me, his leg almost touching mine. I flinch, then try to hide it by saying, "I'm fine with all of this. It's actually delightful to wear shoes that might be haunted." He laughs, and the motion brings him even closer, whipping my chest into a swirl. "If you were dead, would you haunt some bowling shoes?" I stare down at them in all their stained, stinky glory. "If I had nothing better to do." His expression shifts to be more serious.
beats.story_cn: 他和格蕾丝签到时，我才发现他们自带了鞋和球。该死，我这是主动跳进了那个必须穿"千人踩"租赁鞋的深坑。果然，当租赁亭里那位百无聊赖的绅士骄傲地将一双原本可能是白绿相间的旧鞋推过柜台时，我确信第一位租客早些年已自然死亡。在塑料感十足的杯状座椅上系鞋带时，克里夫向我挪近了些，膝盖几乎碰到我的腿。我瑟缩了一下，随即掩饰道："这一切我都OK。穿这种可能闹鬼的鞋子其实挺带感。"他笑起来，这动作让他贴得更近，搅得我胸口一阵翻腾。"如果你死了，会来骚扰这些保龄球鞋吗？"我低头盯着那双沾满污渍、散发着古怪气味的"荣耀战靴"。"要是没别的好做的事，倒未尝不可。"他的神情沉静下来。

beats.story: "So, fair warning: my grandma is a little much. I mean, I love her to death, she raised me on hardly anything, but you know how it is with families?" He says it like it's a question rather than a universal truth. "I didn't mean to rope you into all this." His fingers twitch nervously next to my thigh. This isn't about me. As if on cue, a short lady with curly white hair pouring through a visor approaches in limping steps. She's got Cliff's same cheery eyes paired with a windbreaker suit so bright that the wind knows not to approach from a mile away. She shoves into Cliff and scoops him into her chest, then tilts my way while he suffocates against her bosom. "I'm Lisa, Clifford's granny.
beats.story_cn: “先给你打个预防针：我外婆有点……难搞。当然我爱她爱到骨子里，她当年几乎是一把屎一把尿把我拉扯大，但家庭嘛你懂的？”他说这话时不像陈述事实，倒像个悬而未决的问题。“没想把你也卷进这摊事里。”他的手指在我大腿边神经质地抽搐着。这事跟我无关似的。说时迟那时快，一位烫着蓬松白卷发、护目镜架在头顶的矮个老太太，一瘸一拐地走了过来。她眼睛和克里夫一样弯成月牙，身上那件霓虹色防风衣鲜艳得连风都得绕道三英里。她猛地撞进克里夫怀里，把他整张脸按进胸口，又侧身向我时，他还在她胸怀间憋得喘不上气。“我是丽莎，克利福德的外婆。”

beats.story: "He's always been like that. Even when we were kids, he'd save me his cookies from the government lunch program. Can you imagine that? I like to tell him he's being a bitchy martyr, for balance." My smile is wobbly. I like her, and -- another rush piles through my abdomen, heavier than the last -- I like Cliff. Cliff returns with a giant tray piled high with steaming food that's been through every kind of processing invented. "There's three more trays, so hold tight," he says as he heads back to the counter. He leaves me alone with a giant pile of French fries.

In the corner by the jukebox, there's a young couple looking at songs and laughing and finding little ways to touch each other. This place is so wholesome and lively. A piercing dinging noise suddenly rips through me, sending my skin shivering with goose bumps like an ice cube landed on the back of my neck. I whip around and realize it's coming from a pinball machine, where a dad is playing with his toddler. Reality washes over me, sharp and unbidden. The last time I went bowling was with Ellie. The memory pushes in, as crystalline as if it happened yesterday instead of over a decade ago.

We spent more time making different dirty names for ourselves in the decades-old computer system than actually playing. We were painfully uncool together, but in the best way. A tumbling feeling hits, like sand sifting away inside me. It's like I'm writing over that memory, erasing it.
beats.story_cn: 我们没收到派对邀请，便转而去打保龄。在那台年头久远的电脑系统里，我们耗费的时间远比打球更多——尽是胡编各种粗俗的昵称。我们共享着痛苦却美妙的默契，将"不酷"发挥到极致。最终彻底放弃保龄球，转而用好几局弹球机互较高下。那时距她离世仅剩数月。如今这次将是我的告别之局。某种沉坠感袭来，宛如流沙从我体内簌簌漏尽。仿佛正在覆盖那段记忆，将它擦除。
